name: Prepare for and host accreditation assessments
summary: Each regional laboratory is assessed every two years by one or more accreditation programs (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics ISO 15189 Plus in Ontario, CAP, MANQAP in Manitoba, SCC, and SAMHSA for drug testing). The quality assurance manager runs a readiness project from the notice of the visit: section leads self-assess against several hundred requirements, quality specialists audit records, gaps are fixed and the medical director signs procedures. Peer assessors spend two to three days on site, and the laboratory then has to answer every finding with cause, action and objective evidence by a deadline. Most elapsed time is the notice period and waiting for the accreditor's review, and most effort goes into finding and fixing record gaps such as overdue competency assessments.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with about nine accredited laboratories, several accreditation programs per site and a central quality department with site quality managers.
baseline.notes: One case is one external assessment of one laboratory by one program, from the notice of the visit to the accreditation decision. Corrective actions beyond the response package run in qa-nonconformance-capa.

trigger: The accreditation body confirms an assessment (date, scope and assessor team) for one laboratory, typically about 90 days ahead.
end_state: The accreditor has accepted the corrective action evidence and issued the accreditation decision or surveillance letter, the licence register is updated and the readiness file is closed.

volume.seasonality: None; assessments follow each laboratory's two-year cycle.

evidence.note: Volume taken from the organisation file process map. The licences page lists about 20 accreditations across the laboratories; on two-year cycles plus SAMHSA's periodic inspections that could be 10 or more visits a year, so the process map range may be low (see assumptions).
Organisation file headcount 8 site quality managers; share estimated from the hands-on time below at about six assessments a year, plus continuous readiness work.
The company's quality assurance staff support external inspections by regulators and accreditation bodies (s_dyn_sysval); FTE share is the author's estimate from hands-on time and volume.

roles.title: Charge technologist
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Charge technologists act as section leads for checklist self-assessment and corrective actions; 28 in the organisation file, 9 FTE already claimed by other workflows. Share is the author's estimate from hands-on time.

roles.title: Laboratory manager (discipline)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Discipline managers review section readiness, escort assessors and own root cause work; 7 in the organisation file. Share estimated from hands-on time.

roles.title: Laboratory medical director or clinical scientist (clinical pathologist, biochemist, microbiologist)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Medical directors approve procedures and sign corrective action responses; about 0.06 FTE of the 10 in the organisation file.

roles.title: Vice president, quality and regulatory affairs

evidence.note: Attends closing meetings and signs submissions; small share of one executive.
Licensing and regulatory affairs specialist handles portal submissions, scope and certificates; 2 in the organisation file.

systems.name: Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)
Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Quality control data management software (rules, peer comparison)
Accreditation body client portals (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics QView, CAP e-LAB Solutions Suite)

steps.name: Receive the assessment notice and open a readiness file
steps.description: The quality assurance manager receives the accreditation body's letter or portal notice confirming the assessment dates, scope and assessor team, logs it as a project in the quality management system and informs the vice president, quality, the laboratory director and the discipline managers.
inputs: assessment notice from the accreditation body

evidence.note: Ontario visits are confirmed about 90 days ahead (s_ag2017); CAP inspections outside the US are announced (s_cap_lap). Hands-on time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm scope, test menu and fees with the accreditor
steps.description: The licensing and regulatory affairs specialist compares the laboratory's licence and current test menu with the scope held by the accreditor, updates the activity menu and site contacts in the client portal, and arranges payment of the assessment fee.

error.defect_description: A test added since the last cycle is left out of the scope.

evidence.note: Client portals (CAP e-LAB, AC Diagnostics QView) hold scope and checklists; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Plan readiness and assign checklist sections
steps.description: The quality assurance manager downloads the current requirements and checklists, maps each requirement to a discipline section owner, sets internal deadlines working back from the visit date and holds a kick-off meeting with managers and charge technologists.

error.defect_description: A requirement is assigned to nobody.

evidence.note: Internal audit against the standard and self-inspection as the starting point are described in s_labmgr_17025 and s_cln_2018; hands-on time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review findings from the previous assessment
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist pulls the previous assessment report and the CAPA records it generated, checks that each corrective action was completed and has not recurred, and flags any repeat risk to the section owners.

error.defect_description: A prior finding that recurred is not noticed.

evidence.note: Re-evaluating prior deficiencies and confirming corrective actions were effective is recommended in both sources; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the self-assessment for each checklist section
steps.description: Charge technologists acting as section leads work through every requirement for their discipline, open the procedure, QC, maintenance, competency and proficiency testing records that show compliance, mark each item compliant or not, and note gaps in the self-assessment workbook around their bench duties.

error.defect_description: A gap is marked compliant without checking the record.

evidence.note: Self-assessment is part of the AC Diagnostics cycle (s_acd_journey, s_ag2017); hours across 9 to 12 sections are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Audit document control, competency and PT records
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist samples procedures for current annual review signatures, checks that bench copies match controlled versions, that every technologist's competency assessment is current, that PT attestation pages are signed and graded results were reviewed, and that correlations and maintenance records are complete.

error.defect_description: An overdue competency assessment or unsigned record is missed.

evidence.note: Competency assessment was the top CAP deficiency in 2016, followed by correlations, procedure review and PT evaluation (s_cln_2018); unsigned PT attestations draw deficiencies (s_mlo_eden). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review section results and assign gap fixes
steps.description: Each discipline manager reviews the self-assessment and records audit for their area, decides which gaps can be fixed before the visit and which need a formal CAPA, and assigns each fix with a due date in the tracker.

error.defect_description: A gap is deferred that the assessor will cite.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice in multi-section laboratories.

steps.name: Close gaps before the visit
steps.description: Section leads revise procedures, complete overdue competency assessments, run missing instrument correlations, fill gaps in maintenance logs and retrain staff, then file the evidence in the quality management system against each gap.

error.defect_description: A fix is filed without evidence that it was done.

evidence.note: Corrective action on internal findings before the assessment (s_labmgr_17025); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Medical director approves revised procedures and records
steps.description: The laboratory medical director reviews the revised procedures, method comparison and validation records flagged for signature, approves them electronically in document control or returns them with comments when content is clinically wrong.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus and CAP requirement that the laboratory director approves procedures and their annual review; Accreditation under the Ontario provincial quality management program (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics ISO 15189 Plus), a condition of the Ontario laboratory licence; CAP and MANQAP accreditation where held

evidence.note: Director approval of procedures is a standard accreditation requirement; the return rate and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Submit the self-assessment and pre-visit documents
steps.description: The regulatory affairs specialist uploads the completed self-assessment, quality manual, organisation chart, test menu and any documents the accreditor requested to the client portal before the due date and confirms receipt.

error.defect_description: A requested document is missing from the upload.

control.basis: Accreditor's pre-assessment submission requirements; Accreditation under the Ontario provincial quality management program (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics ISO 15189 Plus), a condition of the Ontario laboratory licence; CAP and MANQAP accreditation where held

evidence.note: Self-assessment and portal submission are part of the AC Diagnostics process; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the assessment date
steps.description: Nothing more is due to the accreditor until the visit; the laboratory waits for the confirmed date while routine testing continues and section leads keep records current.

evidence.note: Visits are confirmed about 90 days ahead (s_ag2017); the share of that window left after preparation is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run a mock assessment and brief staff
steps.description: About two weeks before the visit the quality assurance manager walks each bench with a sample of checklist items, traces a few patient results from requisition to report, asks staff the questions assessors ask and briefs everyone on the agenda and how to answer.

evidence.note: Mock audits and role play are recommended in s_labmgr_17025; hours and the share with gaps are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Fix gaps found in the mock assessment
steps.description: Section leads fix the quick items the mock assessment found, such as an unsigned record, an expired reagent left on a shelf or a staff member unsure where a procedure is kept, and record what was done.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Arrange assessor logistics and records access
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist confirms the agenda with the lead assessor, books rooms, sets up read-only access to the LIS and quality management system, schedules staff for interviews and observation, and assigns an escort to each assessor.

evidence.note: Agreeing the schedule, key staff availability and facility readiness (s_labmgr_17025); times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Escort assessors and answer questions on the benches
steps.description: Over two to three days, discipline managers escort the peer assessors through their sections, open records on request, let them observe testing and interview technologists, and note every concern raised so it can be fixed on site or answered later.

control.basis: External on-site assessment by peer assessors; Accreditation under the Ontario provincial quality management program (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics ISO 15189 Plus), a condition of the Ontario laboratory licence; CAP and MANQAP accreditation where held

evidence.note: Peer inspection teams of practising laboratory professionals (s_cap_lap) and on-site assessment every two years (s_acd_journey); manager hours for a two to four assessor team are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Coordinate the visit and retrieve records for assessors
steps.description: During the visit the quality assurance manager holds daily debriefs with the lead assessor, retrieves records from the quality system and archives within minutes, logs each finding as it is raised and fixes small items on site with documentation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; runs alongside s15.

steps.name: Attend the closing meeting and decide on challenges
steps.description: The vice president, quality, the laboratory director and the quality managers hear the preliminary findings and their grading at the closing meeting, ask for clarification and decide whether any finding should be challenged because the laboratory was compliant at the time.

evidence.note: An average of 15 non-conformances per Ontario visit (s_ag2017) makes a clean visit rare; challenge practice described for CAP; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the written assessment report
steps.description: The accreditor's lead assessor writes up the findings with requirement references and grading and releases the report through the client portal; the response clock usually starts from the visit or the report date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; CAP leaves the deficiency list at the summation conference while AC Diagnostics issues a report afterwards.

steps.name: Log each finding as a nonconformance and assign owners
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist enters every finding in the quality management system as a nonconformance linked to the assessment, sets the response due date and assigns each one to the responsible discipline manager.

error.defect_description: A finding is entered against the wrong section.

evidence.note: About 15 findings per visit on average (s_ag2017), at 10 to 20 minutes each.

steps.name: Investigate causes and plan corrective actions
steps.description: Discipline managers investigate each finding, look for the cause in the process rather than the person, check whether the same gap exists at other sites, and write a corrective action plan with owner and completion date for each finding.

error.defect_description: The cause recorded is superficial (for example retraining only) and the accreditor asks for more.

control.basis: Accreditor requirement that each nonconformity response shows cause, corrective action and evidence; Accreditation under the Ontario provincial quality management program (Accreditation Canada Diagnostics ISO 15189 Plus), a condition of the Ontario laboratory licence; CAP and MANQAP accreditation where held

evidence.note: Plans must address every deficiency with a responsible person and date (s_cln_2018); training deficiency is the most common external root cause and training the most common action (s_yang2026). Hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Implement corrective actions and collect evidence
steps.description: Section leads carry out the actions, such as revising a procedure, retraining staff and recording competency, rerunning a correlation or changing a log sheet, and collect copies of the signed procedure, training records and new records as objective evidence.

error.defect_description: Evidence shows the action was planned but not yet done.

evidence.note: A citation closes only after acceptable evidence of correction (s_cln_2018); hours are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase owners and compile the response package
steps.description: A quality assurance specialist tracks each finding against the deadline, chases owners whose evidence is late, checks that every response states cause, action and evidence, and assembles the package in the format the accreditor requires.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of chasing effort and incomplete evidence share.

steps.name: Medical director reviews and signs the responses
steps.description: The laboratory medical director reads the response package, checks that clinical risks such as possible effects on released patient results are addressed, and signs the responses or sends specific findings back for more work.

control.basis: ISO 15189 Plus and CAP: the laboratory director is responsible for the quality management system and signs off accreditation responses

evidence.note: Director responsibility for the quality system is a standard accreditation requirement; times and return rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Vice president, quality approves the submission
steps.description: The vice president, quality reviews the summary of findings and responses, checks the deadline and any finding with business or licensing risk, and approves the package for submission.

control.basis: Company quality policy that the executive responsible for quality approves submissions to accreditors and regulators

evidence.note: Common practice in multi-site laboratory companies; author's estimate.

steps.name: Upload the evidence to the accreditor portal
steps.description: The regulatory affairs specialist uploads each response and its evidence files to the accreditor's portal against the matching finding, submits before the deadline and saves the confirmation.

error.defect_description: An evidence file is attached to the wrong finding.

control.basis: Accreditor's response deadline (CAP: 30 calendar days from the inspection); late responses delay the accreditation decision

evidence.note: Portal submission (s_acd_home) and evidence-based closure (s_cln_2018); the CAP 30-day deadline is from the author's knowledge of CAP instructions.

steps.name: Wait for the accreditor's review of the evidence
steps.description: The lead assessor reviews each response and its evidence and either accepts it, asks for more evidence on specific findings or, for serious findings, requires a focused follow-up visit before the accreditation decision.

evidence.note: Corrective actions and certificate come about five months after an initial assessment and focused visits can be required for cause (s_acd_journey); acceptance shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Receive the decision and update the licence register
steps.description: When the accreditation decision and certificate or surveillance letter arrive, the regulatory affairs specialist updates the licence and certification register, posts the certificate and sends the report summary to legal and compliance for regulatory reporting.

evidence.note: Certificates issued after corrective actions (s_acd_journey) and published by the company (s_dyn_licences); decision lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the readiness file and report to management review
steps.description: The quality assurance manager closes the readiness project, records lessons learned and open CAPAs, schedules the next self-assessment or surveillance date and summarises the outcome for the quarterly management review.

evidence.note: Management review is part of the company's QMS (s_dyn_licences); times are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Procedures returned by the medical director
exceptions.description: Revised procedures or validation records are sent back before the visit and must be reworked.

exceptions.name: Weak evidence caught internally
exceptions.description: The quality specialist finds evidence that shows an action planned but not done and returns it to the section lead.

exceptions.name: Accreditor asks for more evidence
exceptions.description: The lead assessor rejects one or more responses, so new evidence is collected, signed and resubmitted.

exceptions.name: Focused follow-up visit
exceptions.description: A serious finding requires a focused on-site visit before the decision.

exceptions.name: No findings
exceptions.description: The visit ends with no findings needing a written response.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the confirmed assessment notice to the accreditation decision
benchmarks.population: Accreditation Canada Diagnostics and CAP assessments of Canadian laboratories

evidence.note: About 90 days of notice (s_ag2017) plus about five months from assessment to corrective actions and certificate for AC Diagnostics (s_acd_journey); CAP's 30-day response makes its cases shorter. The p50 and p90 are the author's blend.

benchmarks.unit: findings per on-site visit (Ontario average 2013-2016, range 8 to 28 by region)
benchmarks.population: Ontario licensed laboratories assessed by the Institute for Quality Management in Healthcare

benchmarks.unit: share of applicable requirements met (more than 400 requirements)

pain_points.description: Record gaps (overdue competency assessments, unsigned reviews, missing correlations) are found late, so section leads spend weeks before the visit catching up instead of keeping records current.

evidence.note: Competency assessment, correlations and procedure review top the CAP deficiency list.

pain_points.description: Responses fail because the stated cause is superficial, often 'retrain staff', and evidence shows a plan rather than completed action, so the accreditor asks for more and the decision slips.

evidence.note: Training is the most common corrective action and root cause category in external assessments.

pain_points.description: Several programs (AC Diagnostics, CAP, SCC, SAMHSA, MANQAP) assess the same laboratories on different cycles with different checklists, so the same evidence is prepared several times a year.

evidence.note: Multiple accreditations per laboratory listed on the licences page.

pain_points.description: Bench supervisors do readiness work around full testing workloads, so self-assessment and gap fixes queue for days.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Read from the text copy saved under scratch by earlier work. All licensed laboratories must follow the provincial quality management program of accreditation and proficiency testing (Institute for Quality Management in Healthcare, now Accreditation Canada Diagnostics): on-site assessment every four years, a self-assessment two years after the previous visit (ISO 15189 Plus labs get a surveillance visit at two years instead), next visit confirmed about 90 days ahead. 2012-2016: about 800 non-conformances a year, average 15 per assessment visit (8 to 28 by region), conformance about 97% against more than 400 requirements; most common categories point-of-care testing (17%), laboratory systems for tracking issues with testing (16%), equipment and supplies (12%). Proficiency testing error rate below 1% (0.04% pathology to 1.8% bacteriology). CAP and the Joint Commission make unannounced visits. Community laboratories are not licensed to perform some tests; the Ministry had no process to evaluate new tests for the Schedule of Benefits. Community specimen rejection rates 0.9% and 0.2% in 2016/17.

sources.title: Start your accreditation journey (medical laboratory and diagnostic imaging)
sources.supports: Four-year accreditation cycle with an assessment every two years (surveillance visit at two years, full reassessment at four); self-assessment for new applicants; initial assessment as early as four months after the self-assessment; corrective actions and certificate about five months after the initial assessment; extra focused surveillance visits may be required for cause.

sources.title: Benefits of ISO 15189 Plus through Accreditation Canada Diagnostics
sources.supports: Facilities are assessed against ISO 15189 Plus requirements and receive an external evaluation at the two-year mark; the site links to the QView client portal and an assessor eBinder.

sources.title: Laboratory Accreditation Program
sources.supports: On-site inspections every two years by teams of trained, practising laboratory professionals; checklists updated annually and delivered through e-LAB Solutions Suite; for laboratories outside the US subsequent inspections are announced.

sources.title: Getting ready for your laboratory inspection (P. R. Eden)
sources.supports: Preparation: re-evaluate prior deficiencies and close calls, follow your own SOPs, address every graded PT result and sign PT attestation pages, assess competency by all six methods, maintain point-of-care oversight. CAP inspects unannounced within a three-month window; CLIA requires biennial inspections.

sources.title: Top laboratory deficiencies across accreditation agencies (Chittiprol, Bornhorst, Kiechle)
sources.supports: Competency assessment was the top CAP deficiency in 2016, followed by instrument correlations and method comparisons, procedure manual review, PT evaluation and maintenance records. Self-inspection recommended. A CMS plan of correction is due within 10 business days, must address every deficiency with a responsible person and completion date, and compliance is expected within 30 to 45 days; a citation closes only after acceptable evidence of correction.

sources.title: Preparing for an ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation assessment (J. Mensingh)
sources.supports: Preparation steps: internal audit of management and technical requirements, corrective action on internal findings before the visit, review of past findings, document and record readiness, staff training and mock audits, agreeing the schedule and key staff availability, pre-assessment meeting.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: Accreditations by laboratory: Accreditation Canada ISO 15189 (Brampton, London, Ottawa, Peterborough), CAP (Brampton, London, Ottawa, Winnipeg, Impact Genetics), SCC ISO 15189 and ISO/IEC 17025 (Laval, Brampton, London, Edmonton), SAMHSA (London, Edmonton), MANQAP (Winnipeg), provincial licences. QMS components include management review, internal corporate quality audits, preventive and corrective action programs, equipment validation, change control and computerized systems validation, document and record control, and external quality assessment for all assays (CAP, QMP-LS, Healthmetrix).

sources.title: Current list of HHS-certified laboratories and instrumented initial testing facilities (notice 2026-10884)
sources.publisher: Federal Register (US Department of Health and Human Services)
sources.supports: Certified laboratories must take part in a quarterly performance testing program and undergo periodic on-site inspections; lists the model laboratory, London, Ontario as a certified urine laboratory and the model laboratory Edmonton as an IITF.

sources.title: Manager, System Validations (job posting, Brampton)
sources.supports: Leads the System Validation Analysts in quality assurance, who validate information system changes for new assay methods, products and equipment across the LIS (AS400, Omnitech, national order entry, middleware, LabDirector, MedLab) and result outputs (EMRs, eResults, OLIS); product owner of the electronic QMS for document, occurrence and equipment management; supports external inspections by regulators, accreditation bodies and clients; internal audits and periodic reviews of information systems. Salary CAD 72,000 to 90,000.

sources.title: The 'Double Helix' model of quality monitoring during initial ISO 15189 implementation (Yang et al.)
sources.publisher: PLoS One (record read through Europe PMC)
sources.supports: One laboratory, 2021-2024: 35 internal-audit and 67 external-assessment nonconformities. Root causes: personnel negligence (40%) and training deficiencies (31%) internally; training deficiencies (40%) and document and record deficiencies (22%) externally. Personnel training was the most common corrective action (47% internal, 41% external). External assessments raised more nonconformities than internal audits.

assumptions: The process map triggers this process with an accreditation_report from the accreditation body; the organisation file has no separate 'assessment notice' object, so the notice is treated as the first document of the report cycle and the written findings arrive at s18.

Volume follows the organisation file (0.2 to 1 assessment a month). The licences page shows about 20 accreditations across the laboratories and SAMHSA certification requires periodic on-site inspections (s_fr_nlcp), which suggests 10 or more external visits a year; the smaller SAMHSA and SCC surveillance visits may be under-counted in the process map.

The workflow describes a full Accreditation Canada Diagnostics or CAP assessment. Surveillance years with a self-assessment only, and SAMHSA semiannual inspections, follow the same steps with less effort.

Controls tied to accreditation are marked fixed_by_law because Ontario licensing requires participation in the provincial quality management program (s_ag2017); in Manitoba and Quebec the equivalent requirements come from MANQAP and provincial licensing.

Hands-on time totals about 600 to 650 hours per assessment across all roles (simulated median about 620); with 0.5 assessments a month that is about 2.5 FTE, spread thinly across many people. Continuous readiness work outside an assessment cycle is not counted.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
The 30-day CAP response deadline is stated from the author's knowledge of CAP instructions; the CAP PDF could not be read, so the step evidence is tier B through the general sources.
